Alice M.: Quick heads-up — ran a 30m replay of last week's prod traces through the harness and we got non-negligible perf divergence vs the synthetic load.
Ben R.: What kind of divergence? latency, throughput, correctness?
Alice M.: Mainly p95 latency and kernel selection differences under sustained load. Also some KV cache cold-start behavior that synthetic tests didn't show.
Carla P.: Can you paste the command you used?
Alice M.: `./replay --trace=prod_2026-03-15.tgz --seed=2026 --mode=exact-routing --duration=1800`
Sam (infra-bot): Replay job 1784321101 started on pool gpu-dedicated-7.
Ben R.: Interesting. Which kernels were different?
Alice M.: We saw switch from `attn_fused_v2` to `attn_emulated` after about 2 minutes in some workers. Looks like sequence length distribution drifted and kernel selector picked safer fallback.
Jon K.: That matches a packing/batching heuristic issue — when batch shapes become heterogeneous the selector prefers the robust kernel.
Maria L.: Did you capture profiler samples?
Alice M.: Yeah — short flame sample. paste:```
CPU 64.3% memcpy
GPU kernel_launch 18.1%
Kernel selector path: 12.4%
KV cache lookup 3.2%
```
Carla P.: memcpy hot path suggests bad batching alignment or too much tensor copy between CPU/GPU. Could be our replay harness not using the same colocated producer pattern as prod.
Ben R.: Did you warm up KV cache? Synthetic replays usually include a warmup phase that primes prefix caches. If you replay cold, first N tokens will thrash.
Alice M.: I intentionally disabled warmup to see worst-case, but we should run a warmed pass. Cold run p95 = 420ms, warmed pass p95 = 140ms (same trace, same config).
Jon K.: That delta is huge and explains some parity failures vs synthetic. For apples-to-apples we need the replay harness to mimic production client patterns: session affinity, prefix reuse, and request inter-arrival variance.
Maria L.: Also need to check sampling. Current harness sampled uniformly over sessions; prod has heavy-tail long sessions. We should stratify sampling by session length and peak token/sec.
Carla P.: Agreed. Without stratified sampling kernel selector sees different seq-lens and picks different kernels. That breaks comparisons when we toggle quantization or batching heuristics.
Ben R.: Any determinism concerns? If kernel selection is non-deterministic across workers we might get divergence solely from order of requests.
Alice M.: We observed node-to-node variability even with `--seed`. Probable causes: nondeterministic kernel tie-breakers and slight differences in batch packing order. Also different CUDA driver versions on canaries.
Jon K.: Proposed mitigations: 1) add a replay warmup step that issues the first 30s of each session (to prime KV), 2) use deterministic packing in harness (stable sort by session id + timestamp), 3) pin kernel selector flags for golden runs.
Maria L.: Also add a parity check layer that compares top-3 token choices and p50/p95 latency buckets between golden and candidate runs. If top-3 mismatch > 0.5% or p95 regression > 10% fail.
Carla P.: Suggest we log the kernel name selected per request in the harness so we can correlate kernel flips with latency spikes. Something like `kernel_selected=attn_emulated` in replay log lines.
Ben R.: Can we get a tiny example of the log snippet?
Alice M.: Sure: `2026-03-16T08:12:31Z session=usr_123 req=457 kernel_selected=attn_fused_v2 batch_shape=[8,512] kv_hit=true latency_ms=112`
Sam (infra-bot): Replay job 1784321101 completed: 30m, 6.2M tokens, avg qps=34.
Jon K.: Next steps I propose: run three runs on the same commit: golden (pin kernel + warmed KV), candidate A (batching heuristics on), candidate B (batching heuristics + quantization). Collect per-request kernel tag, kv_hit flag, and latency percentiles.
Maria L.: Also capture hardware/drivers and python/CUDA runtime versions in run metadata to avoid false diffs.
Carla P.: One more: make harness emulate client inter-arrival jitter. Right now our synthetic driver issues at fixed intervals — that changes batch formation.
Ben R.: I'll draft the experiment script. Alice, can you attach the raw profiler and the small list of sessions that exhibited the biggest kernel flips?
Alice M.: Uploading to /internal/replays/1784321123/ now. Included a short reproducer trace (first 200 sessions) and the profiler tar.
Jon K.: Ok let's aim to run the three comparisons tomorrow on canary pool and then a single golden run on prod-dedicated. If parity checks fail we gate the heuristic rollout.
Maria L.: +1. Put the success criteria in the PR: top-3 token parity >= 99.5% and p95 not worse than 5% for warmed runs.
Carla P.: I'll update the replay harness to include deterministic packing and kernel tag logging. ETA EOD.
Ben R.: Thanks all. This is a good catch — shows why synthetic-only benchmarks miss production behavior.
Alice M.: Agreed. Will post results once the three runs finish. :eyes:
